publishedDocument.description: A warm visual identity, waitlist landing page, and sponsorship package for an outdoor builder retreat.

details.label: Focus
details.value: Visual identity · Landing page · Editorial design

publishedDocument.intro: SummerHacks imagines a hackathon outside the familiar classroom setting: a builder retreat inspired by summer camp. The design work translates that idea into a warm visual identity, an early waitlist landing page, and a sponsorship package.
publishedDocument.overview: As Co-Director of SummerHacks, I worked on the way the event introduces itself to participants and partners. The work includes nature-inspired graphic explorations, landing-page concepts, and several versions of a sponsorship document.

children.text: Warm orange, cream, and pale blue connect the work to sunlight, open air, and summer. Fruit, leaves, flowers, and campsite-inspired forms appear in the graphic library, creating a set of elements that can move between digital and printed material.

Large typography and generous space keep the identity approachable. The sponsorship cover pairs a simple wordmark with an oversized organic form and the line “Where the brightest ideas meet the brightest stars.”

content.alt: SummerHacks sponsorship package cover with nature-inspired graphics
content.caption: Sponsorship package cover

sections.heading: Build the identity around the setting.
sections.title: Visual identity

children.text: The landing-page concept gives SummerHacks the largest visual presence, with sunset imagery and a curved graphic occupying the edge of the screen. The email waitlist is the primary action.
The page uses a small amount of copy to establish the atmosphere and invitation. This provides a focused entry point while the broader event format is developed in the sponsorship materials.

sections.heading: Make the first interaction a simple invitation.
sections.title: Landing page

children.text: The sponsorship package explores a sequence from the event vision and snapshot to audience, partnership tiers, and contact information. Repeated headings, page labels, and illustrated motifs connect the presentation to the landing page.

Multiple versions show the format being refined across editorial layouts and sponsorship tables. The resulting design direction links an outdoor event concept with a clear structure for prospective partners.

sections.title: Sponsorship
